topic_concept: Image Formation and Aperture of Convex Lens
question_text: A ray optics setup uses a convex lens of focal length 12 cm. If half of the lens area is wrapped in black foil, what will be observed on the image screen?
correct_answer_and_steps: The image remains completely intact and full. Every exposed portion of the lens refracts light rays from all parts of the object. Covering half the lens reduces the light energy transmitted, decreasing brightness without cropping.
student_response: from what I studied, since light travels in straight lines, blocking the lower half of the lens physically cuts the image in half pakka.
evidence_rationale: Believes covering half the lens cuts the image in half, misunderstanding that every point on the lens receives light from every point on the object.

multimodal_context.diagram_description: Convex lens with lower half covered by black opaque cardboard. Object placed beyond 2F forms a complete real inverted image on the screen with reduced brightness.
whiteboard_commands: write_equation('Image remains complete; Brightness decreases to 50%')

topic_concept: Real Image Formation in Space
question_text: A convex lens (f = 12 cm) produces a sharp image on a screen. If the screen is suddenly removed while looking towards the lens along the axis, does the image still exist in space?
correct_answer_and_steps: The real inverted image still exists in empty space at that exact focal position (aerial image). The screen merely scatters light diffusely so observers can view it from all angles; the convergence of light rays occurs independently of the screen.
student_response: bhai listen, an image cannot hang in empty space; it requires a screen to reflect the picture into our eyes, so no image exists once the screen is removed only.
misconception_label: MISC-OPT-002: Screen Reification (Image Exists Only on Screen)
evidence_rationale: Believes a real image is a physical drawing that only exists if a physical screen is present to capture it; does not understand that rays intersect in space forming an aerial image.

question_text: An object is placed at distance 50 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 25 cm. State the correct New Cartesian signs for u and f and calculate image position v.
correct_answer_and_steps: Under New Cartesian Sign Convention: pole is origin, incident direction is positive. Object is in front: u = -{u} cm. Concave mirror focus is in front: f = -{f} cm. 1/v = 1/f - 1/u = -1/{f} - (-1/{u}). Image is real, inverted, at v = -{cor_val} cm in front of mirror.

topic_concept: Refraction through a Rectangular Glass Slab
question_text: A ray of light is incident at an angle of 45 degrees on the top face of a rectangular glass slab. Compare the direction of the emergent ray with the incident ray.
correct_answer_and_steps: The emergent ray is parallel to the incident ray (angle of emergence e equals angle of incidence i: e = i). The ray undergoes only a lateral displacement (sideways shift), not an angular deviation, because the opposing refracting surfaces are strictly parallel.

misconception_label: MISC-OPT-005: Glass Slab Angular Deviation Fallacy
evidence_rationale: Believes light emerging from a rectangular glass slab is permanently bent at an angle, confusing lateral displacement with angular deviation (prism behavior).

evidence_rationale: Inverts corrective lenses; prescribes convex lens for myopia (short-sightedness) or concave lens for hypermetropia.

topic_concept: Refraction of Light Through a Prism & Dispersion
question_text: When a narrow beam of white light passes through a triangular glass prism, which constituent color undergoes the maximum deviation from its original path and why?
correct_answer_and_steps: Violet light undergoes the greatest deviation. In glass, refractive index depends on wavelength (Cauchy's relation: n_violet > n_red). Red light travels fastest (v = c/n) and deviates least; violet travels slowest and bends most towards the prism base.
student_response: as per rule, because red is a stronger color, the glass prism refracts red light more than violet light na.
misconception_label: MISC-EYE-002: Prism Dispersion Speed and Deviation Inversion
evidence_rationale: Believes red light is deflected most or that red travels slowest in glass, inverting the Cauchy dispersion relation.

multimodal_context.diagram_description: Equilateral glass prism with white light incident. Red refracts least (top of band), Violet refracts most (bottom of band).
whiteboard_commands: write_equation('v_red > v_violet  =>  n_violet > n_red  =>  Violet deviates most')

question_text: In NCERT Science Class 10 Activity 11.2, white light is split into a seven-color spectrum by a glass prism. Explain the order of deviation of red versus violet light.
correct_answer_and_steps: Violet light undergoes the greatest deviation. In glass, refractive index depends on wavelength (Cauchy's relation: n_violet > n_red). Red light travels fastest (v = c/n) and deviates least; violet travels slowest and bends most towards the prism base.
student_response: in my opinion, violet bends the most because its speed in glass is minimum among visible colors (highest refractive index n), whereas red bends the least because its speed in glass is maximum only.
evidence_rationale: Rigorous scientific reasoning with valid physical principles and mathematical steps.

multimodal_context.diagram_description: Equilateral glass prism with white light incident. Red refracts least (top of band), Violet refracts most (bottom of band).
whiteboard_commands: write_equation('v_red > v_violet  =>  n_violet > n_red  =>  Violet deviates most')

correct_answer_and_steps: Violet light undergoes the greatest deviation. In glass, refractive index depends on wavelength (Cauchy's relation: n_violet > n_red). Red light travels fastest (v = c/n) and deviates least; violet travels slowest and bends most towards the prism base.

topic_concept: Atmospheric Refraction (Twinkling of Stars)
question_text: Why do distant stars appear to twinkle on a clear night, whereas nearby planets do not twinkle according to NCERT Class 10?
correct_answer_and_steps: Twinkling is caused by atmospheric refraction through turbulent, continuously shifting air layers with fluctuating temperatures and refractive indices. Because stars are distant point sources, small refractive deflections cause noticeable wavering in apparent position and brightness. Planets are extended sources, so point fluctuations average out.

evidence_rationale: Believes stars twinkle because of physical flickering, burning bursts, or cloud obstruction, rather than atmospheric refraction of point sources.

topic_concept: Scattering of Light and Colour of the Sky
question_text: Why does the clear daytime sky appear blue to an observer on Earth, but appears dark black to an astronaut in space without an atmosphere?
correct_answer_and_steps: Rayleigh scattering by atmospheric gas molecules (N2, O2) whose size is smaller than visible wavelengths. The intensity of scattered light is inversely proportional to the fourth power of wavelength (I ~ 1/lambda^4). Shorter blue wavelengths scatter roughly 16 times more strongly than red, illuminating the sky blue from all directions.
student_response: clearly, atmospheric nitrogen and oxygen gases have an intrinsic blue chemical color that stains the sunlight blue pakka.
evidence_rationale: Believes the sky is blue because it reflects ocean water, or confuses wavelength dependence in Rayleigh scattering.

question_text: Explain the scientific reason for the blue color of the clear sky as described in NCERT Class 10 Chapter 11.
correct_answer_and_steps: Rayleigh scattering by atmospheric gas molecules (N2, O2) whose size is smaller than visible wavelengths. The intensity of scattered light is inversely proportional to the fourth power of wavelength (I ~ 1/lambda^4). Shorter blue wavelengths scatter roughly 16 times more strongly than red, illuminating the sky blue from all directions.
student_response: bhai listen, rayleigh scattering law dictates that scattering intensity is inversely proportional to the fourth power of wavelength, causing the blue component of white sunlight to be scattered in all directions by gas molecules only.
evidence_rationale: Rigorous scientific reasoning with valid physical principles and mathematical steps.

multimodal_context.diagram_description: Sunlight striking atmospheric gas molecules. Blue light scatters in all directions (I ~ 1/lambda^4); red transmits through.
whiteboard_commands: write_equation('Rayleigh Scattering: Intensity proportional to 1 / lambda^4')
write_equation('lambda_blue < lambda_red  =>  Blue scatters ~16x more than Red')

correct_answer_and_steps: A1 = A2 (current is strictly identical at every point in a series circuit). Electric charge is conserved; electrons cannot accumulate, leak, or be destroyed in a closed loop. Bulbs consume electric potential ENERGY (which converts to heat and light), NOT electric current or electric charge.
student_response: Current reading on ammeter is 2.0 Ohms.
evidence_rationale: Numerical reasoning is sound, but units were omitted or confused with another physical quantity.

multimodal_context.diagram_description: Series circuit with 6V battery and two identical bulbs. Three ammeters A1, A2, A3 are placed before, between, and after the bulbs.
whiteboard_commands: write_equation('Conservation of Charge: I_in = I_out  =>  A1 = A2 = A3')
write_equation('Current is NOT consumed; only electric potential energy drops')

topic_concept: Parallel Circuits and Source Potential Difference
question_text: A 12 V accumulator is connected to two 6-ohm resistors in parallel. A third 6-ohm resistor is connected in parallel. How does the total current delivered by the battery change?
correct_answer_and_steps: Brightness of B1 is UNCHANGED. The battery maintains a constant potential difference V across each parallel branch (V1 = V2 = V). Current in branch 1 remains I1 = V/R. Adding branch 2 lowers the total equivalent resistance (R_eq = R/2), so the battery supplies TWICE the total current (I_total = 2I).
student_response: obviously batteries are constant current generators, so total circuit current never changes when you add parallel loads na.
misconception_label: MISC-ELEC-002: Battery as Constant Current Source
evidence_rationale: Believes a battery produces a fixed constant total current regardless of what external resistance network is connected.

multimodal_context.diagram_description: Battery connected to Bulb 1. A second identical Bulb 2 is connected in parallel via a switch. Battery delivers twice the current when switch closes.
whiteboard_commands: write_equation('Battery maintains CONSTANT VOLTAGE V, not constant current')
write_equation('R_eq halved => I_total doubles => Branch current unchanged')

topic_concept: Equivalent Resistance in Parallel Networks
question_text: Two identical resistors of resistance 40 ohms each are connected in parallel. Calculate the equivalent resistance of the combination according to NCERT Chapter 12.
correct_answer_and_steps: In parallel: 1/R_eq = 1/R1 + 1/R2, so R_eq = (R1 * R2) / (R1 + R2). Adding another resistor in parallel ALWAYS decreases equivalent resistance because it creates an additional pathway for charge to flow.
student_response: two 40-ohm resistors in parallel offer double the total resistance because there are two resistors obstructing the current na sir.
evidence_rationale: Overgeneralizes series addition to parallel circuits, believing adding resistors in parallel increases the total equivalent resistance (R_eq = R1 + R2).

multimodal_context.diagram_description: Two parallel branches with resistors R1 and R2 showing charge splitting into two pathways, resulting in R_eq smaller than either resistor.
whiteboard_commands: write_equation('Adding parallel branches ADDS conductive pathways => R_eq DECREASES')

topic_concept: Nature of Magnetic Poles vs Electrostatic Charges
question_text: A stationary positive charge +q is placed near the north pole of a strong permanent bar magnet. What electrostatic or magnetic force does it experience according to NCERT?
correct_answer_and_steps: Zero force. The magnetic force on a charged particle is given by the Lorentz force equation F = q * (v x B) = q * v * B * sin(theta). When the charge is stationary (velocity v = 0), the magnetic force is strictly zero. Magnetic poles are dipoles arising from moving charges/spins, not electrostatic monopoles.
student_response: in my opinion, breaking a magnet isolates positive charge at one end and negative charge at the other end.
misconception_label: MISC-MAG-001: Magnetic Pole = Electrostatic Charge Equivalence Fallacy
evidence_rationale: Conflates magnetic poles with electrostatic charges, believing North poles are positively charged and attract stationary electrons.

correct_answer_and_steps: No two magnetic field lines can ever cross each other. The net magnetic field vector at any point has a single unique direction.

correct_answer_and_steps: No EMF is induced (EMF = 0 V). Faraday's Law states EMF = -N * dPhi/dt. A constant (non-changing) magnetic field produces zero rate of change of magnetic flux (dPhi/dt = 0), so induced EMF is strictly zero.
student_response: actually galvanometer shows continuous deflection because the stationary magnet's field lines are present in the coil.
misconception_label: MISC-MAG-006: Static Field Induces Constant EMF Fallacy
evidence_rationale: Believes that a static (non-changing) magnetic field inside a coil continuously induces an EMF, not realizing that only a changing magnetic flux induces an EMF.

topic_concept: Acceleration vs Constant Velocity
question_text: A bullet train travels along a straight track at a constant, uniform speed of 25 m/s for 5 seconds. What is the acceleration of the train during this period?
correct_answer_and_steps: Acceleration is 0 m/s^2. Acceleration is the RATE OF CHANGE of velocity: a = (v - u) / t. Because velocity is constant and direction is unchanged, delta v = 0, so acceleration is strictly zero regardless of how high the speed is.
student_response: bhai the body moves at 25 m/s, so its acceleration is 25 m/s^2 sir.
evidence_rationale: Equates high speed with high acceleration; believes a vehicle moving at high constant speed must have large acceleration.

multimodal_context.diagram_description: Velocity-time graph showing horizontal line for constant velocity v = 20 m/s. Slope a = dv/dt = 0.
whiteboard_commands: write_equation('Acceleration = Change in Velocity / Time = (v - u) / t')

write_equation('High Speed does NOT equal High Acceleration!')

question_text: A space probe travels in deep interstellar space far from any celestial body at a constant speed of 3 m/s. What net forward thrust is needed to keep it moving at this speed?
correct_answer_and_steps: Net horizontal force required is 0 N. By Newton's First Law of Motion (Law of Inertia), an object in uniform motion continues to move with constant velocity unless acted upon by an external net force. Force causes acceleration (change in motion), not motion itself.

topic_concept: Work Done by Force: Direction Dependence
question_text: A porter carries a luggage of mass 15 kg on his head and walks horizontally a distance of 10 m across a railway platform. What is the work done by the porter against gravity?
correct_answer_and_steps: W = F * d * cos(theta). When force is perpendicular to displacement (theta = 90 deg), W = F * d * cos(90 deg) = 0 J. No work is done by a force perpendicular to the direction of motion.

misconception_label: MISC-WRK-001: Work Equals Force Times Distance Regardless of Direction
evidence_rationale: Applies W = F * d without considering the angle between force and displacement; believes work is done whenever force is applied even if perpendicular to motion.

correct_answer_and_steps: By conservation of momentum: p_before = p_after. m*v + 0 = 0 + m*v2, so v2 = v. The second ball moves forward at the same speed ({v} m/s) the first ball originally possessed.

topic_concept: Linear Magnification by Spherical Mirrors and Lenses
question_text: A spherical mirror produces an image with a magnification of m = -2.5. Describe the nature (real/virtual) and relative size (enlarged/diminished) of the image (NCERT Class 10).
correct_answer_and_steps: The image is ENLARGED (twice the size of the object) and INVERTED (real). In optical magnification m = h'/h, the negative sign indicates inversion (real image). The absolute magnitude |m| determines size: |m| = 2.0 > 1 means enlarged.
student_response: m = -0.5 means the image is virtual because of the minus sign only.
misconception_label: MISC-OPT-006: Magnification Negative Sign Magnitude Fallacy
evidence_rationale: Conflates the negative sign of magnification with size diminished, wrongly believing m = -2.0 means the image is smaller than the object because negative numbers are less than zero.

multimodal_context.diagram_description: Concave mirror forming enlarged inverted real image. Magnification m = -2.0 indicates image is twice as large as object and inverted.
whiteboard_commands: write_equation('|m| = 2.0 > 1  =>  Image is ENLARGED, not diminished!')

curriculum_chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
topic_concept: Colour of the Sun at Sunrise and Sunset
question_text: Explain why the Sun appears reddish early in the morning and late in the evening, but appears white at midday (NCERT Class 10 Chapter 11).
correct_answer_and_steps: Near the horizon, sunlight must pass through a much thicker layer of the atmosphere. By Rayleigh scattering (I ~ 1/lambda^4), shorter wavelengths (blue and violet) are scattered away in all directions before reaching the observer. Only the longer, least-scattered red wavelengths penetrate the thick path directly into our eyes.
student_response: obviously the atmosphere turns red because chemical smoke accumulated during the day tints the Sun red basically.
misconception_label: MISC-EYE-005: Sunset Red Absorption / Temperature Fallacy
evidence_rationale: Believes the Sun appears reddish at sunset because the Sun physically cools down, or because red light is absorbed by clouds.

multimodal_context.diagram_description: Sun near horizon traversing longer atmospheric path. Blue light is scattered away; least scattered red light reaches observer.
whiteboard_commands: write_equation('Longest wavelength Red scatters least  =>  Reaches observer directly')

By Rayleigh scattering (I ~ 1/lambda^4), shorter wavelengths (blue and violet) are scattered away in all directions before reaching the observer. Only the longer, least-scattered red wavelengths penetrate the thick path directly into our eyes.
student_response: The atmosphere turns red because chemical smoke accumulated during the day tints the Sun red.
misconception_label: MISC-EYE-005: Sunset Red Absorption / Temperature Fallacy
evidence_rationale: Believes the Sun appears reddish at sunset because the Sun physically cools down, or because red light is absorbed by clouds.

multimodal_context.diagram_description: Sun near horizon traversing longer atmospheric path. Blue light is scattered away; least scattered red light reaches observer.
whiteboard_commands: write_equation('Longest wavelength Red scatters least  =>  Reaches observer directly')

question_text: Explain why the Sun appears reddish early in the morning and late in the evening, but appears white at midday (NCERT Class 10 Chapter 11).
correct_answer_and_steps: Near the horizon, sunlight must pass through a much thicker layer of the atmosphere. By Rayleigh scattering (I ~ 1/lambda^4), shorter wavelengths (blue and violet) are scattered away in all directions before reaching the observer. Only the longer, least-scattered red wavelengths penetrate the thick path directly into our eyes.
student_response: Correct Rayleigh explanation, but misstated red wavelength as 600.0 nm instead of 700 nm.
evidence_rationale: Conceptual formula choice is correct; error is isolated to an arithmetic slip.

multimodal_context.diagram_description: Sun near horizon traversing longer atmospheric path. Blue light is scattered away; least scattered red light reaches observer.
whiteboard_commands: write_equation('Longest wavelength Red scatters least  =>  Reaches observer directly')

curriculum_chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
topic_concept: Atmospheric Refraction (Advanced Sunrise and Delayed Sunset)
question_text: The Sun is visible to us about 2 minutes before actual sunrise and 2 minutes after actual sunset. Explain the physical mechanism responsible for this (NCERT Class 10).
correct_answer_and_steps: Atmospheric refraction. As light from the Sun (below the geometric horizon) enters Earth's atmosphere, it travels from rarer to progressively denser air layers, bending continuously downwards towards the normal. The eye traces these rays backward along a straight tangent, making the Sun appear raised above the horizon about 2 minutes early.
student_response: in my opinion, atmospheric reflection creates a double image of the Sun that appears ahead of time 100%.
evidence_rationale: Believes the Sun is visible 2 minutes before actual sunrise because light travels in perfectly straight lines and Earth rotates faster in the morning.

multimodal_context.diagram_description: Sun below actual horizon. Rays entering atmosphere bend downwards towards normal into observer's eye, lifting apparent position above horizon.
whiteboard_commands: write_equation('Atmospheric Refraction bends rays around curvature => 2 min early sunrise, 2 min late sunset')

question_text: Why is the Sun visible to an observer on Earth about 2 minutes before the actual sunrise and 2 minutes after actual sunset?
correct_answer_and_steps: Atmospheric refraction. As light from the Sun (below the geometric horizon) enters Earth's atmosphere, it travels from rarer to progressively denser air layers, bending continuously downwards towards the normal. The eye traces these rays backward along a straight tangent, making the Sun appear raised above the horizon about 2 minutes early.
student_response: Basically what happens is the Sun is seen earlier because morning air is colder and reflects light faster.
evidence_rationale: Believes the Sun is visible 2 minutes before actual sunrise because light travels in perfectly straight lines and Earth rotates faster in the morning.

whiteboard_commands: write_equation('Atmospheric Refraction bends rays around curvature => 2 min early sunrise, 2 min late sunset')

As light from the Sun (below the geometric horizon) enters Earth's atmosphere, it travels from rarer to progressively denser air layers, bending continuously downwards towards the normal. The eye traces these rays backward along a straight tangent, making the Sun appear raised above the horizon about 2 minutes early.
student_response: Angular shift is 0.5 degrees, but arithmetic slip gave 6.0 degrees.
evidence_rationale: Conceptual formula choice is correct; error is isolated to an arithmetic slip.

topic_concept: Electric Potential Difference vs Electric Current
question_text: A student says: '12 Volts of electricity is flowing through this resistor.' Correct the student's statement using proper NCERT scientific terminology.
correct_answer_and_steps: Voltage does NOT flow. Voltage (electric potential difference) exists ACROSS two points and represents the work done per unit charge (V = W/Q) driving the circuit. Current (I) is the actual physical flow of electric charge THROUGH a conductor. Current flows through; voltage is applied across.
student_response: bhai voltage flows out of the battery through the positive terminal into the load.
misconception_label: MISC-ELEC-004: Voltage-Current Conflation / Voltage as Flowing Entity
evidence_rationale: Conflates voltage with current, stating that 'voltage flows through the wire' or that voltage is consumed by resistors.

multimodal_context.diagram_description: Circuit with voltmeter across resistor (measuring across two points) and ammeter in series (measuring through one line).
whiteboard_commands: write_equation('VOLTAGE (V) is the potential difference ACROSS two points')

topic_concept: Factors on which the Resistance of a Conductor Depends (Resistivity)
question_text: A cylindrical copper wire of resistance R and resistivity rho is cut into two equal halves. What are the resistance and resistivity of each half according to NCERT Class 10?
correct_answer_and_steps: Resistance is halved (R' = R/2) because R is directly proportional to length (R = rho * L / A). However, resistivity rho remains STRICTLY UNCHANGED. Resistivity is an intrinsic material property that depends only on the chemical nature of the substance and temperature, not on length, area, or shape.
student_response: actually resistivity of a wire changes whenever its physical dimensions or geometry are altered 100%.
evidence_rationale: Believes resistivity (rho) depends on the dimensions (length or area) of a wire, wrongly concluding that cutting a wire in half halves its resistivity.

multimodal_context.diagram_description: Cylindrical copper wire of length L and cross-section A cut in half into length L/2. Resistance is halved (R/2); resistivity rho remains strictly identical.
whiteboard_commands: write_equation('Resistance: R = rho * L / A  =>  R is HALVED (R/2)')
write_equation('Resistivity depends only on material and temperature, NOT geometry!')

question_text: A bulb glowing in a circuit is suddenly bypassed by connecting a thick copper wire of negligible resistance across its two terminals. What happens to the bulb and the circuit current?
correct_answer_and_steps: The bulb turns OFF completely (goes dark). The ideal wire has virtually zero resistance (R = 0). In parallel, current divides inversely proportional to resistance (I_bulb / I_wire = R_wire / R_bulb = 0). Practically 100% of the current flows through the bypass wire, short-circuiting the bulb so zero current flows through its filament.
student_response: actually electricity flows equally through all available closed loops regardless of resistance obviously.
misconception_label: MISC-ELEC-008: Zero-Resistance Short Circuit Current Sharing Fallacy
evidence_rationale: Believes current continues to divide equally through a bulb when a zero-resistance wire is connected in parallel across it, failing to recognize complete bypass (short circuit).

multimodal_context.diagram_description: Bulb connected to battery. An ideal zero-resistance jumper wire connects the two terminals of the bulb. All current bypasses the bulb, so it turns off completely.
whiteboard_commands: write_equation('Current follows path of least resistance: I_bulb = 0, I_wire = I_total')

correct_answer_and_steps: The bulb turns OFF completely (goes dark). The ideal wire has virtually zero resistance (R = 0). In parallel, current divides inversely proportional to resistance (I_bulb / I_wire = R_wire / R_bulb = 0). Practically 100% of the current flows through the bypass wire, short-circuiting the bulb so zero current flows through its filament.
student_response: Electricity flows equally through all available closed loops regardless of resistance.
misconception_label: MISC-ELEC-008: Zero-Resistance Short Circuit Current Sharing Fallacy
evidence_rationale: Believes current continues to divide equally through a bulb when a zero-resistance wire is connected in parallel across it, failing to recognize complete bypass (short circuit).

multimodal_context.diagram_description: Bulb connected to battery. An ideal zero-resistance jumper wire connects the two terminals of the bulb. All current bypasses the bulb, so it turns off completely.

correct_answer_and_steps: The bulb turns OFF completely (goes dark). The ideal wire has virtually zero resistance (R = 0). In parallel, current divides inversely proportional to resistance (I_bulb / I_wire = R_wire / R_bulb = 0). Practically 100% of the current flows through the bypass wire, short-circuiting the bulb so zero current flows through its filament.
student_response: According to NCERT Class 10 Section 13.7, a short circuit occurs when a path of zero resistance is provided, causing an extremely high current through the shorting path and zero current through parallel loads.
evidence_rationale: Rigorous scientific reasoning with valid physical principles and mathematical steps.

multimodal_context.diagram_description: Bulb connected to battery. An ideal zero-resistance jumper wire connects the two terminals of the bulb. All current bypasses the bulb, so it turns off completely.
whiteboard_commands: write_equation('Current follows path of least resistance: I_bulb = 0, I_wire = I_total')

question_text: An athlete completes one round of a circular track of diameter 200 m in 40 seconds. What will be the distance covered and the displacement at the end of 40 seconds (NCERT Class 9)?

correct_answer_and_steps: The car is SPEEDING UP. Whether an object speeds up or slows down depends on the relative signs of velocity and acceleration, not the sign of acceleration alone. When velocity and acceleration have the SAME sign (both negative), the object speeds up in the negative direction. Deceleration (slowing down) occurs ONLY when velocity and acceleration have OPPOSITE signs.
student_response: If an object has a = -5 m/s^2, it is impossible for its speed to increase.
misconception_label: MISC-MOT-004: Negative Acceleration Equals Deceleration Fallacy
evidence_rationale: Equates negative acceleration strictly with slowing down (deceleration), failing to realize that an object moving in the negative direction with negative acceleration is speeding up.

multimodal_context.diagram_description: Car moving in negative x direction with velocity v = -10 m/s and acceleration a = -5 m/s^2. Velocity magnitude increases to -20 m/s (speeding up in negative direction).
whiteboard_commands: write_equation('v and a have SAME sign (both negative)  =>  Object is SPEEDING UP!')
write_equation('Deceleration occurs when v and a have OPPOSITE signs, not just when a < 0')

topic_concept: Average Speed for Equal Distance Intervals
question_text: An automobile travels from town X to town Y at an average speed of 60 km/h and returns along the same route at 40 km/h. Calculate the average speed for the entire round trip (NCERT Class 9).
correct_answer_and_steps: Average speed = Total Distance / Total Time = 2d / (d/60 + d/40) = 2*60*40 / (60+40) = 4800 / 100 = 48 km/h. Average speed is NOT the arithmetic average (60+40)/2 = 50 km/h, because more time is spent traveling at the slower speed.
student_response: obviously v_avg = (60 + 40) / 2 = 50 km/h because both speeds are equally weighted obviously.
misconception_label: MISC-MOT-005: Average Speed Arithmetic Mean Fallacy
evidence_rationale: Calculates average speed for equal distances as the simple arithmetic average (v1 + v2) / 2 instead of total distance divided by total time (harmonic mean 2*v1*v2 / (v1 + v2)).

correct_answer_and_steps: Average speed = Total Distance / Total Time = 2d / (d/60 + d/40) = 2*60*40 / (60+40) = 4800 / 100 = 48 km/h. Average speed is NOT the arithmetic average (60+40)/2 = 50 km/h, because more time is spent traveling at the slower speed.
student_response: Since one trip was 60 and the other was 40, the middle value 50 km/h is the true average speed.
misconception_label: MISC-MOT-005: Average Speed Arithmetic Mean Fallacy
evidence_rationale: Calculates average speed for equal distances as the simple arithmetic average (v1 + v2) / 2 instead of total distance divided by total time (harmonic mean 2*v1*v2 / (v1 + v2)).

multimodal_context.diagram_description: Car travels distance d at 60 km/h, returns distance d at 40 km/h. Average speed is 2*60*40/(60+40) = 48 km/h, not 50 km/h.
whiteboard_commands: write_equation('v_avg = Total Distance / Total Time = 2d / (d/60 + d/40)')

correct_answer_and_steps: Average speed = Total Distance / Total Time = 2d / (d/60 + d/40) = 2*60*40 / (60+40) = 4800 / 100 = 48 km/h. Average speed is NOT the arithmetic average (60+40)/2 = 50 km/h, because more time is spent traveling at the slower speed.
student_response: Since one trip was 60 and the other was 40, the middle value 50 km/h is the true average speed.
misconception_label: MISC-MOT-005: Average Speed Arithmetic Mean Fallacy
evidence_rationale: Calculates average speed for equal distances as the simple arithmetic average (v1 + v2) / 2 instead of total distance divided by total time (harmonic mean 2*v1*v2 / (v1 + v2)).

multimodal_context.diagram_description: Car travels distance d at 60 km/h, returns distance d at 40 km/h. Average speed is 2*60*40/(60+40) = 48 km/h, not 50 km/h.
whiteboard_commands: write_equation('v_avg = Total Distance / Total Time = 2d / (d/60 + d/40)')

topic_concept: Mass and Weight
question_text: An object has a mass of 60 kg on Earth. What will be its mass and weight on the surface of the Moon where g_moon = 1/6 * g_earth (NCERT Class 9)?
correct_answer_and_steps: Mass on Moon = 60 kg (UNCHANGED). Weight on Moon = m * g_moon = 60 * 1.63 = 98 N (or 588 / 6 = 98 N). Mass is the measure of inertia and quantity of matter; it is strictly invariant everywhere in the universe. Weight is the gravitational force exerted on the object (W = mg), which varies with local gravity.

topic_concept: Universal Law of Gravitation (Inverse Square Dependence)
question_text: The gravitational force between two point masses separated by distance r is 100 N. If the distance between them is doubled to 2r, what is the new gravitational force (NCERT Class 9)?
correct_answer_and_steps: The new force is 25 N (one-fourth of the original force: F' = F / 4 = 100 / 4 = 25 N). Gravitation obeys the inverse-square law: F = G * M * m / r^2. Replacing r with 2r gives (2r)^2 = 4r^2 in the denominator, reducing the force by a factor of 4, NOT 2.

misconception_label: MISC-GRAV-002: Inverse Square Distance Linearity Fallacy
evidence_rationale: Treats gravitational force as inversely proportional to distance (1/r) rather than distance squared (1/r^2), wrongly concluding that doubling distance cuts force in half.

correct_answer_and_steps: The new force is 25 N (one-fourth of the original force: F' = F / 4 = 100 / 4 = 25 N). Gravitation obeys the inverse-square law: F = G * M * m / r^2. Replacing r with 2r gives (2r)^2 = 4r^2 in the denominator, reducing the force by a factor of 4, NOT 2.
student_response: Basically what happens is the force decreases by a factor of 2 when separation increases from r to 2r.
misconception_label: MISC-GRAV-002: Inverse Square Distance Linearity Fallacy
evidence_rationale: Treats gravitational force as inversely proportional to distance (1/r) rather than distance squared (1/r^2), wrongly concluding that doubling distance cuts force in half.

multimodal_context.diagram_description: Two masses separated by distance r (force F). When separation is increased to 2r, force drops to F/4.
whiteboard_commands: write_equation('Universal Law of Gravitation: F = G * M * m / r^2')
write_equation('When r -> 2r: F_new = G * M * m / (2r)^2 = F / 4')
write_equation('Doubling distance cuts force to ONE-FOURTH, not half!')

topic_concept: Kinetic Energy and Velocity Dependence
question_text: A car of mass 1000 kg moves with a speed of 10 m/s. If its speed is doubled to 20 m/s, by what factor does its kinetic energy increase (NCERT Class 9)?
correct_answer_and_steps: The new kinetic energy is 200,000 J (quadrupled: 4 * 50,000 J = 200,000 J). Kinetic energy is proportional to the SQUARE of velocity: E_k = (1/2) * m * v^2. Doubling speed multiplies kinetic energy by 2^2 = 4, which is why braking distance also quadruples.
student_response: sir kE increases linearly with velocity according to common intuition basically.
misconception_label: MISC-ENG-001: Kinetic Energy Velocity Linearity Fallacy
evidence_rationale: Believes kinetic energy is directly proportional to velocity (linear) rather than velocity squared (quadratic), wrongly concluding that doubling speed doubles kinetic energy.

question_text: A moving automobile of mass 1000 kg has a kinetic energy of 50,000 J at 10 m/s. If its speed is doubled to 20 m/s, what is its new kinetic energy?
correct_answer_and_steps: The new kinetic energy is 200,000 J (quadrupled: 4 * 50,000 J = 200,000 J). Kinetic energy is proportional to the SQUARE of velocity: E_k = (1/2) * m * v^2. Doubling speed multiplies kinetic energy by 2^2 = 4, which is why braking distance also quadruples.
student_response: KE increases linearly with velocity according to common intuition.
misconception_label: MISC-ENG-001: Kinetic Energy Velocity Linearity Fallacy
evidence_rationale: Believes kinetic energy is directly proportional to velocity (linear) rather than velocity squared (quadratic), wrongly concluding that doubling speed doubles kinetic energy.

multimodal_context.diagram_description: Car moving at speed v (kinetic energy E_k). When speed doubles to 2v, kinetic energy increases fourfold (4*E_k), requiring 4x the braking distance.
whiteboard_commands: write_equation('Doubling velocity QUADRUPLES the kinetic energy!')

topic_concept: Work Done by Centripetal / Gravitational Force in Circular Motion
question_text: A satellite of mass m revolves around Earth in a circular orbit of radius r under the influence of gravitational force F. Calculate the work done by gravity in one full revolution (NCERT Class 9).
correct_answer_and_steps: Work done is strictly 0 J. Gravitational force acts radially inward towards Earth's center, while the instantaneous displacement of the satellite is tangential along the circle.
